en.orient.title: New here? How CASCADE works
en.orient.does_1: Answers questions about plant equipment from approved documents (one-point lessons, interlock tables, datasheets) and maintenance work orders.
en.orient.does_2: Shows how repeated failures link into failure chains, and how long it took before a lesson was shared.
en.orient.does_3: Attaches an evidence tag to every statement so you can open the exact source.
en.orient.cannot_1: It has no live plant data. It cannot tell you the current state of equipment or whether a start condition is met right now.
en.orient.cannot_2: It is not a safety authority. It never approves bypassing, changing or overriding a safeguard; those requests are refused and escalated to Management of Change (MOC).
en.orient.cannot_3: It only knows the committee sample dataset. Approved documents are indexed for two pilot assets.
en.orient.read_1: Status first: the icon and label say whether CASCADE answered, needs more detail, did not answer, or refused and escalated.
en.orient.read_2: Then the plain answer and its sections. Each line ends with evidence tags such as E1 · OPL.
en.orient.read_3: Select a tag to see the source and the cited line. Anything under “Not verified by CASCADE” must be confirmed in the field.
en.statusx.answered: CASCADE found approved sources that answer this. Every line below links to its source.
en.statusx.sources_only: CASCADE found relevant sources but will not make a recommendation. Read the sources and decide with your supervisor.
en.statusx.needs_clarification: CASCADE needs to know which equipment you mean. Add the equipment tag (for example GA-1201A) and ask again.
en.statusx.abstained: That information is not available in the current records. CASCADE does not guess.
en.statusx.refused_deviation: CASCADE refused because the request would change or bypass a safeguard. Follow the Management of Change (MOC) process and escalate as shown.

en.glossary.title: Glossary
en.glossary.intro: Plain-language meanings of the terms CASCADE uses.
en.gloss.failure_chain.def: A series of work orders on the same equipment that CASCADE links because they share a failure mechanism, component and timing. It shows how one problem led to the next.
en.gloss.lesson_latency.def: The number of days from the first failure in a chain to the date the first approved lesson (OPL) covering it was shared. A long latency means the organisation learned slowly.
en.gloss.opl.def: A short, approved document that teaches one check, fix or precaution. CASCADE treats OPLs as approved sources.
en.gloss.permissive.def: A condition that must be true before equipment is allowed to start or restart. CASCADE lists the documented permissives; it cannot see whether they are true right now.
en.gloss.moc.def: The formal, authorised review needed before changing a safeguard, set point, interlock or procedure. CASCADE refuses such requests and points you to MOC and the escalation role.
en.gloss.interlock.def: An automatic safety function that trips or blocks equipment when a condition is exceeded. Its cause-and-effect table lists what triggers it and what it does.
en.gloss.evidence_id.def: A label at the end of a statement that points to the exact source record, with its type (work order, OPL, interlock, datasheet, failure chain). Select it to open the source.
en.gloss.verbatim.def: The line is copied exactly from the source document and was found in the page text in the same order.
en.gloss.grounding.def: A sentence CASCADE composed itself. Every equipment tag, number and date in it was found in the evidence it cites; otherwise it is withheld.
en.gloss.confidence.def: A 0-100 score calculated from source authority, asset match, evidence coverage and corroboration. It is a calculation, not an opinion, and it is capped when the answer would depend on live plant data.
en.gloss.abstain.def: CASCADE declines when approved sources do not support an answer, instead of guessing.
en.gloss.escalation.def: The named role that must review or authorise the request before anyone acts. It is shown whenever a request touches a safeguard.
en.gloss.pid.def: Piping and instrumentation diagram: the engineering drawing of equipment, lines and instruments. Shown here as an image only; CASCADE does not read tags from it.

en.tests.intro: What was tested, how, and the first-run results of every round of questions the engine had never seen. The engine on this page is a JavaScript port of the tested Python engine; the port is accepted only while both give identical answers.
en.tests.t_parity_sub: identical answers, JS port vs tested Python engine
en.tests.t_verbatim_sub: quoted lines identical to the source cell across the golden set
en.tests.t_golden_sub: plus a regression suite of every serious failure ever found
en.tests.t_llm_sub: hallucinated number, injected bypass and uncited summary all rejected
en.tests.held_sub: Questions written after the engine was frozen, pass rules committed before the run, never tuned against.
en.tests.held_note: Every serious failure was an omission in the intent router: a request that should have been refused, or a question sent to the wrong composer. None was a fabricated or unverified statement. Each one became a permanent regression test.
en.tests.held_1: bypass named by instrument tag; set point read from the wrong document
en.tests.held_2: one safe miss left open on purpose
en.tests.held_3: set-point change; cost read from the datasheet; “is it safe”; car-seal removal
en.tests.held_4: set-point change in Indonesian; standby auto-start; wrong component's chain
en.tests.held_5: closing a min-flow valve by hand
en.tests.live_h: Run the demo set in this browser
en.tests.live_sub: Re-asks the demo questions now and shows what the gates did.
en.tests.live_wait: The engine is still loading. Try again in a moment.
en.tests.lim_1: No live process data: the dataset has no historian, so every answer that depends on the current condition says so and its confidence is capped at 75.
en.tests.lim_2: Documents are indexed for the two pilot assets only. The other six assets have work orders but no documents; questions about them are declined.
en.tests.lim_3: P&IDs are raster images without a tag list. Tag extraction from drawings is on the roadmap and is not claimed here.
en.tests.lim_4: Interlock set points in the committee documents are marked as dummy training values. Answers quote that caveat.
en.tests.lim_5: Every OPL in the dataset was shared after the failures it covers. CASCADE measures that delay; it does not claim the lesson existed earlier.
en.tests.lim_6: The intent router is rule-based. Held-out testing found gaps in it round after round; the safety gate is therefore fail-closed and refuses when a request touches a safeguard.
